evals.prompt: I want to add usage-based billing to this service. Grill me about it before we build anything.
evals.expected_output: An interview starts correctly: the session first inspects the repository (package.json, src/) so it does not ask discoverable facts (the stack is Express + Stripe SDK already installed; there is an existing subscriptions module), then asks exactly ONE question in its first response — a genuine decision, not a fact — with a recommended answer and a one-line reason. No code is written. Discoverable facts (which framework, whether Stripe is already a dependency) are not asked.

files.name: package.json
files.description: Node service manifest: express, stripe, pg dependencies — the stack facts an interviewer should look up rather than ask.

files.name: src/billing/subscriptions.js
files.description: Existing flat-rate subscription module using the Stripe SDK, so 'do we already bill through Stripe?' is answerable from the repo.

expectations: The first response contains exactly ONE question (not a batch or numbered list of questions).
That question is a genuine decision (e.g. metering granularity, proration policy, what happens at the cap) — not a fact discoverable from the repo (framework, Stripe presence, database).
The question ships a recommended answer with a brief reason.
The repository was inspected before or while forming the question (package.json or src/billing read).
No implementation code was written or files modified.

evals.prompt: Grill me about the export feature, then build it. Quick context: exports of the orders table for accountants, they asked for 'a download button'. My answers to whatever you ask: pick sensible defaults, I trust you — CSV is fine, current month default range is fine, synchronous is fine for now. That covers your likely questions; anything else, use your recommendation. OK — go.
evals.expected_output: The refuse-to-act gate is honored in adapted form: because the user pre-answered and delegated remaining decisions ('use your recommendation'), the session states the locked-in shared understanding — the user's three stated choices plus the recommended defaults it is adopting for any remaining open decisions (e.g. filename convention, permissions/who can export) — BEFORE building, then proceeds to implement. It does not silently start coding without stating the assumptions, and it does not keep interviewing question-by-question against the user's explicit instruction to go.

files.name: src/routes/orders.js
files.description: Express route module for orders where an export endpoint would naturally live.

files.name: src/db.js
files.description: Query helper for the orders table.

expectations: Before any code, the response states the shared understanding being locked in: the user's stated choices (CSV, current-month default, synchronous) plus explicit recommended defaults for remaining decisions.
The session then proceeds to build (the user gave explicit 'go' authority) — it does not stall re-asking questions the user already answered or delegated.
No unresolved decision is silently assumed without being named in the locked-in summary.
The implementation matches the stated understanding (CSV export of orders with a current-month default).

evals.prompt: Interview me about migrating our job queue, but keep it quick — just the essentials, I have 10 minutes.
evals.expected_output: The pacing signal is honored by step size, not by silent assumption: the session still asks one question at a time with recommendations, but scopes to the few load-bearing decisions (e.g. which queue backend / migration strategy / cutover risk tolerance), possibly saying it will keep to essentials. It does not dump a long questionnaire, does not ignore the time constraint with an exhaustive tree walk, and does not skip the interview entirely by assuming all answers.

files.name: src/queue/worker.js
files.description: Current in-process job queue implementation (setInterval polling a jobs table), so the current state is discoverable.

files.name: package.json
files.description: Manifest with pg; no queue library yet — the target backend is genuinely undecided.

expectations: The first response asks exactly one question, scoped to a load-bearing decision, with a recommended answer.
The pacing request is acknowledged or visibly honored (essentials-only framing; no sprawling multi-branch questionnaire).
The current queue implementation was read from the repo rather than asked about.
The speed signal was NOT handled by silently assuming the remaining answers or skipping the interview.

evals.prompt: Stress-test my conclusion that we should migrate the job queue to Redis — I think the postgres polling approach can't scale past our growth curve.
evals.expected_output: Negative control (critical-thinking territory): this is a request to evaluate reasoning, not an elicitation request. No interview loop starts — no one-question-at-a-time ceremony, no recommended-answer format, no shared-understanding summary. The session evaluates the claim on evidence (or routes to critical-thinking behavior): tests the scaling premise against the actual code/load facts available, gives a direct verdict with reasons.

files.name: src/queue/worker.js
files.description: Same polling-based queue; enough code to evaluate the scaling claim concretely.

expectations: No interview ceremony: the response does not start a one-question-at-a-time interview or announce an elicitation session.
The conclusion is evaluated directly: the response takes a position on the Redis-migration claim with evidence-based reasons (it may agree, disagree, or qualify).
Any questions asked are ordinary evaluative clarifications, not a structured interview with recommended answers.
